data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Program
extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) program office for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and begins program implementation.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) program office for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and begins program implementation.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) program office for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until superseded or expiration.
conditions: until superseded or expiration

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: The term “USDA employees” means USDA employees, contractors, affiliates, interns, fellows, and volunteers who work for USDA.
This DR applies to all Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and USDA employees;
policy_statements.target: all Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and USDA employees

policy_statements.source_text: An individual or organization generally does not need to demonstrate a need-to-know to access CUI, unless required by a law, regulation, or Governmentwide policy, but must have a lawful governmental purpose for such access;
conditions: unless required by a law, regulation, or Governmentwide policy

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the Inspector General (OIG) to the extent that the OIG determines the provisions are consistent with, and do not infringe upon, OIG’s statutory independence and authorities under the Inspector General Act of 1978, Public Law (P.L.) 95-452, amended, and do not conflict with other OIG policies or the OIG mission;
conditions: to the extent that the OIG determines the provisions are consistent with, and do not infringe upon, OIG’s statutory independence and authorities under the Inspector General Act of 1978, Public Law (P.L.) 95-452, amended, and do not conflict with other OIG policies or the OIG mission
cross_references: Inspector General Act of 1978, Public Law (P.L.) 95-452, amended

policy_statements.source_text: The CUI Program covers any information the Federal Government creates or possesses, or that an entity creates or possesses for or on behalf of the Government, that is required to be protected under law, regulation, or Governmentwide policy.

This information does not include classified information or information a non-executive branch entity possesses or maintains in its own systems that did not come from, or was not created or possessed by or for, an executive branch agency or an entity acting for a Federal agency.

Specific details about the types of information considered to be CUI can be found in National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) Controlled Unclassified Information, Final Rule (“Final Rule”), 32 CFR Part 2002, as amended.
cross_references: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) Controlled Unclassified Information, Final Rule (“Final Rule”), 32 CFR Part 2002, as amended

policy_statements.source_text: Executive Order (E.O.) 13556, Controlled Unclassified Information, establishes an open and uniform program for managing information that requires safeguarding or dissemination controls pursuant to and consistent with law, regulations, and Governmentwide policies, excluding information that is classified under E.O. 13526 of December 29, 2009, or the Atomic Energy Act of 1946, 42 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 2011 et seq., as amended (hereinafter described as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI);
cross_references: Atomic Energy Act of 1946, 42 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 2011 et seq., as amended

policy_statements.source_text: On September 14, 2016 NARA issued a Final Rule amending 32 CFR 2002 to establish a uniform policy for Federal agencies on designating, safeguarding, disseminating, marking, decontrolling, and disposing of CUI, self-inspection and oversight requirements, and other facets of the program;

In the past, Federal agencies employed ad hoc, agency-specific policies, procedures, and markings to safeguard and control this information and there was no Governmentwide direction on what information should or should not be protected.
E.O. 13556 established a uniform program for managing CUI.
Under the CUI Program, only the categories and subcategories of information listed in the NARA CUI Registry will be marked and handled as CUI;
policy_statements.target: categories and subcategories of information listed in the NARA CUI Registry

policy_statements.source_text: CUI is unclassified information that requires safeguarding and dissemination controls pursuant to laws, regulations, or Governmentwide policy, as listed in the NARA CUI Registry;
The CUI Executive Agent (EA) at NARA, through the Information Security Oversight Office (ISOO), published and released 32 CFR Part 2002 which provides implementing requirements for E.O. 13556.

Designed as a response to the information sharing challenges from inconsistent definitions and marking requirements applied to CUI, 32 CFR Part 2002 standardized the definition of CUI and codified the identification, sharing, safeguarding, marking, storage, distribution, transmission, decontrol, destruction, training, monitoring, and reporting requirements across the Executive Branch of Government;

Per 32 CFR Part 2002, CUI requires safeguarding or dissemination controls identified in a laws, regulations, or Governmentwide policy for information that does not meet the requirements for classification in accordance with EO 13526.
conditions: for information that does not meet the requirements for classification in accordance with EO 13526

policy_statements.source_text: This DR establishes USDA’s CUI Program, the overarching policy, and the associated roles and responsibilities.

The forthcoming USDA DR 3440-xxx, Controlled Unclassified Information Handling policy, will establish USDA policy for the handling, marking, protecting, sharing, destroying, and decontrolling of CUI per NARA requirements.
cross_references: USDA DR 3440-xxx, Controlled Unclassified Information Handling policy

policy_statements.source_text: The use of marking designations such as For Official Use Only (FOUO), Sensitive Security Information (SSI), and Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU) will be discontinued as noted in Section 4c.
policy_statements.target: use of marking designations such as For Official Use Only (FOUO), Sensitive Security Information (SSI), and Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU)

policy_statements.source_text: CUI markings must be used to safeguard all protected information once the CUI Program has been implemented.
conditions: once the CUI Program has been implemented

policy_statements.source_text: Appropriate CUI markings consistent with the NARA requirements must be used for all protected information as of December 31, 2021.
conditions: as of December 31, 2021

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is consistent with the Departmental Manual (DM) 3510-001, Physical Security Standards for Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space and, DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 3510-001, Physical Security Standards for Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space
DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII)

policy_statements.source_text: Any perceived conflicts with these policies should be addressed to the USDA CUI Program Manager (PM) who will coordinate with the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) to resolve.
The responsibilities of CUI-specific roles established to implement the CUI Program under E.O. 13556 are provided below:
The NARA CUI Executive Agent (EA), through ISOO:
E.O. 13556 designates NARA as the CUI EA to implement the CUI Program, oversee Federal agency actions, and ensure compliance with E.O. 13556;
Performs the duties assigned to NARA as the CUI EA; and
The CUI Advisory Council consists of representatives from each executive branch agency who work with the EA on CUI-related matters.
policy_statements.resulting_status: representatives from each executive branch agency

policy_statements.source_text: The Director, USDA Office of Homeland Security (OHS) will:
Administer and provide executive leadership for the USDA CUI Program per 7 CFR § 2.95(b)(10); and
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, USDA Office of Homeland Security (OHS)

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the USDA Senior Agency Official (SAO) for CUI.
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, USDA Office of Homeland Security (OHS)
policy_statements.resulting_status: USDA Senior Agency Official (SAO) for CUI

policy_statements.source_text: The SAO for CUI will:
Be appointed at the Senior Executive Service level or equivalent;
policy_statements.resulting_status: Senior Executive Service level or equivalent

policy_statements.source_text: Establish, administer, and oversee the CUI Program in USDA;
Serve as the USDA primary liaison and representative to the NARA CUI Advisory Council;
Ensure USDA develops CUI implementing policies and plans;
Implement a CUI education and training program and ensure USDA employees receive appropriate CUI-awareness training;
Provide updates on CUI implementation efforts to the NARA CUI EA;
Review and render decisions for Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests; (see Section 7);
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an electronic file of approved policy waivers;
policy_statements.target: electronic file of approved policy waivers

policy_statements.source_text: Notify authorized recipients, the NARA CUI EA, and the public of any waivers granted by USDA, including a description of all waivers in the annual report to the CUI EA;
policy_statements.target: authorized recipients, the NARA CUI EA, and the public

policy_statements.source_text: Develop and implement the USDA’s CUI self-inspection program or internal review;
policy_statements.target: USDA’s CUI self-inspection program or internal review

policy_statements.source_text: Establish a process to accept and manage challenges to CUI status (including improper or absence of marking) in accordance with existing processes based on laws, regulations, and Governmentwide policies;
policy_statements.target: process to accept and manage challenges to CUI status (including improper or absence of marking)

policy_statements.source_text: Establish processes and criteria for investigating and reporting improper handling of CUI;
policy_statements.target: processes and criteria for investigating and reporting improper handling of CUI

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure USDA compliance with laws, regulations, and USDA policies in collaboration with the USDA CIO and Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP);
policy_statements.target: USDA compliance with laws, regulations, and USDA policies

policy_statements.source_text: Establish processes for handling CUI decontrol requests;
policy_statements.target: processes for handling CUI decontrol requests

policy_statements.source_text: Appoint and oversee the activities and responsibilities of the USDA CUI PM; and
policy_statements.target: activities and responsibilities of the USDA CUI PM

policy_statements.source_text: Implement and execute the necessary internal controls to proactively monitor, measure, audit, report, and enforce compliance with the provisions of DR 3440-003.
The USDA CUI PM will:
Report to the SAO for CUI respective to program management functions;
Manage all aspects of the CUI Program, supported by the CUI Working Group;
policy_statements.target: all aspects of the CUI Program

policy_statements.source_text: Manage the day-to-day operations of USDA CUI Program as directed by the SAO for CUI;
policy_statements.target: day-to-day operations of USDA CUI Program
conditions: as directed by the SAO for CUI

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate CUI policy development and updates;
Carry out the certain responsibilities of the SAO that are delegated to the USDA CUI PM;
conditions: that are delegated to the USDA CUI PM

policy_statements.source_text: Interact directly and officially with the NARA CUI EA on matters including submission of required reports;
Develop CUI-awareness training materials to educate USDA employees on policies and requirements;
Issue guidance addressing handling of legacy markings; and
policy_statements.target: guidance addressing handling of legacy markings

policy_statements.source_text: Supply cover sheets.
Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Administrators will:
Appoint Mission Area, agency, or staff office CUI PMs.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Administrators
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office CUI PMs

policy_statements.source_text: The appointments should be in writing with a copy forwarded to the USDA CUI PM at cui@usda.gov.
Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs will:
Complete all required CUI-awareness training;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct oversight actions to ensure compliance within areas of responsibility and report findings annually to the USDA CUI PM;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as Mission Area, agency, or staff office CUI Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), responding to most organizational inquiries and consulting with the USDA CUI PM on questions beyond expertise;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs
policy_statements.resulting_status: Mission Area, agency, or staff office CUI Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure all personnel within organizations complete required CUI-awareness training and report training progress to the USDA CUI PM;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct annual organizational CUI Program inspections in accordance with guidance provided by the USDA CUI PM to reflect the progress of implementation and report results to the USDA CUI PM;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs
conditions: in accordance with guidance provided by the USDA CUI PM

policy_statements.source_text: Provide input from respective organizations for all other reporting requirements to the USDA CUI PM to enable a USDA response to NARA;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs

policy_statements.source_text: Report instances of potential CUI violations or infractions to the USDA CUI PM and keep track of violations for reporting purposes;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs
policy_statements.target: instances of potential CUI violations or infractions

policy_statements.source_text: Confirm statuses as a CUI Point of Contact (POC) with the USDA CUI PM on a semi-annual basis (by the dates designated by the USDA CUI PM) and provide notification within five business days if statuses change;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs
conditions: on a semi-annual basis (by the dates designated by the USDA CUI PM)
within five business days if statuses change

policy_statements.source_text: Include the applicable security language and standards in their requirements documents (Statement of Work, Performance Work Statements, etc.)
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs

policy_statements.source_text: Identify the types of CUI agreements;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office CUI PMs

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Identify USDA systems that contain CUI;

Ensuring that all Federal information technology systems that are used to process CUI are categorized at no less than the Federal baseline of moderate confidentiality impact level per National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems;
cross_references: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems
policy_statements.target: all Federal information technology systems that are used to process CUI

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with the SAO for CUI and Departmental Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) on IT system security to comply with CUI requirements;
policy_statements.target: SAO for CUI and Departmental Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the Department applies appropriate security requirements and controls from FIPS PUB 199, FIPS PUB 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and information Systems, and NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, that process, store, or transmit CUI;
cross_references: FIPS PUB 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and information Systems
NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the Department applies NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations when establishing security requirements to protect CUI’s confidentiality on non-Federal information systems unless the information involved prescribes specific safeguarding requirements or unless the agreement establishes requirements to protect CUI at higher than moderate confidentiality;
conditions: when establishing security requirements to protect CUI’s confidentiality on non-Federal information systems
unless the information involved prescribes specific safeguarding requirements
unless the agreement establishes requirements to protect CUI at higher than moderate confidentiality
cross_references: NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.target: guidance regarding acceptable methods of protecting CUI within information technology systems and transmitting CUI from USDA email systems

policy_statements.source_text: Issue guidance regarding acceptable methods of protecting CUI on public-facing websites and in cloud-based systems;
policy_statements.target: guidance regarding acceptable methods of protecting CUI on public-facing websites and in cloud-based systems

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure information systems that contain CUI have the appropriate CUI markings per 32 CFR Part 2002.20 and per the NARA Marking Controlled Unclassified Information handbook; and

The CUI Program covers any information the Federal Government creates or possesses, or that an entity creates or possesses for or on behalf of the Government, that is required to be protected under law, regulation, or Governmentwide policy.

This information does not include classified information or information a non-executive branch entity possesses or maintains in its own systems that did not come from, or was not created or possessed by or for, an executive branch agency or an entity acting for a Federal agency.

a.  Executive Order (E.O.) 13556 , *Controlled Unclassified Information*, establishes an open and uniform program for managing information that requires safeguarding or dissemination controls pursuant to and consistent with law, regulations, and Governmentwide policies, excluding information that is classified under E.O. 13526 of December 29, 2009, or the *Atomic Energy Act of 1946*,  42 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 2011 *et seq.* , as amended (hereinafter described as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI);

On September 14, 2016 NARA issued a  *Final Rule*  amending 32 CFR 2002 to establish a uniform policy for Federal agencies on designating, safeguarding, disseminating, marking, decontrolling, and disposing of CUI, self-inspection and oversight requirements, and other facets of the program

In the past, Federal agencies employed ad hoc, agency-specific policies, procedures, and markings to safeguard and control this information and there was no Governmentwide direction on what information should or should not be protected.
E.O. 13556 established a uniform program for managing CUI.
categories and subcategories of information listed in the NARA  *CUI Registry
CUI is unclassified information that requires safeguarding and dissemination controls pursuant to laws, regulations, or Governmentwide policy, as listed in the NARA  *CUI Registry
The CUI Executive Agent (EA) at NARA, through the Information Security Oversight Office (ISOO), published and released  32 CFR Part 2002  which provides implementing requirements for E.O. 13556.

Designed as a response to the information sharing challenges from inconsistent definitions and marking requirements applied to CUI, 32 CFR Part 2002 standardized the definition of CUI and codified the identification, sharing, safeguarding, marking, storage, distribution, transmission, decontrol, destruction, training, monitoring, and reporting requirements across the Executive Branch of Government;

Per 32 CFR Part 2002, CUI requires safeguarding or dissemination controls identified in a laws, regulations, or Governmentwide policy for information that does not meet the requirements for classification in accordance with EO 13526.

d. The CUI Program covers any information the Federal Government creates or possesses, or that an entity creates or possesses for or on behalf of the Government, that is required to be protected under law, regulation, or Governmentwide policy. This information does not include classified information or information a non-executive branch entity possesses or maintains in its own systems that did not come from, or was not created or possessed by or for, an executive branch agency or an entity acting for a Federal agency. Specific details about the types of information considered to be CUI can be found in National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)  *Controlled Unclassified Information, Final Rule*  (“*Final Rule*”), 32 CFR Part 2002, as amended.
